name: @12-apps/frontend-harness
$comment:build-before-test: playwright.config.ts serves dist/ with `vite preview`, so a run WITHOUT a preceding build silently validates a STALE bundle — green on code that is no longer there. That is not hypothetical: it hid a page added by a merge (12-17's lifecycle-admin) behind 11 'element not found' timeouts, and before that it let a run report 164 passed against a bundle predating the changes under test. These scripts used to own the build, which covered every entrypoint EXCEPT the one a person debugging reaches for: `npx playwright test <one-spec>` walked straight past them. So the build moved into playwright.config.ts's webServer command — the only way anything starts the SPA — and must NOT be repeated here: two owners of one guarantee doubles the cost of every run and is how the uncovered path appeared in the first place.
description: Consumer harness: a real app built against the PUBLISHED tarballs, never against the workspace. scripts/harness-install.mjs turns this into package.json by adding the @12-apps dependencies as file: tarballs — which is why the @12-apps names are absent here rather than pinned to a version nobody would remember to bump.
//peers: react-router-dom and @tanstack/react-query are PEERS of @12-apps/report-builder, not conveniences. Its react entry re-exports pages that import them, so the barrel must resolve them at build time even when the harness renders only a component that needs neither. A real consumer of that entry has both installed — which is what this harness exists to replicate.
//backend: This SPA has no backend of its own and depends on `hono` for nothing. The reports surface is answered by harness/backend — a real server, on a real port, over a real Postgres — which vite.config.ts proxies `/api` to. `hono` used to be here because the package's OWN router was mounted INSIDE the browser: isomorphic, no socket, and so no request left the tab and no save survived a reload.
